overview: This surviving page is a list-of-papers or routing sheet for correspondence concerning the Turkish Government’s expulsion of Japanese press correspondents. It summarizes three telegrams from Turkey: two November reports about the expulsion of Eti Moto, a Nichi Nichi Shimbun correspondent accused of photographing military zones, and a January report about the expulsion of a Domei agency correspondent from Istanbul. The underlying telegrams are listed but are not present in the supplied file text.

subfiles.title: List of papers on expelled Japanese correspondents in Turkey
subfiles.about: An index sheet records three diplomatic telegrams concerning the expulsion of Japanese news correspondents from Turkey and Istanbul.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a November 19 telegram from Honaker reporting the expulsion of Eti Moto, a Nichi Nichi Shimbun correspondent accused of photographing military zones. It also records Kelley’s November 20 report conveying a Turkish Press Bureau official’s explanation for the expulsion. A third entry identifies a January 29 telegram from Steinhardt in Ankara about the expulsion of a Domei agency correspondent from Istanbul.

interest: The sheet provides a compact record of Turkish action against Japanese news-gathering personnel and shows how alleged photography in restricted military areas could become a diplomatic and press issue. It is especially useful for identifying three otherwise absent telegrams, their senders, dates, subjects, and departmental routing. The pairing of the Nichi Nichi Shimbun and Domei cases may help historians trace wartime surveillance of Japanese correspondents and restrictions on foreign reporting in Turkey.
